speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing right groin pain and had an abnormal leg position after a rear-end collision. To assess the extent of your injury, can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and if you heard a "pop" at the time of the accident?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. You mentioned pain in both knees and severe right groin pain; specifically, could you describe the exact nature of the groin pain (sharp vs. dull) and if it radiates down your thigh or leg? Additionally, are you currently able to bear weight on the right leg?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Femoral Neck Fracture

The patient's leg is shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated, which is the classic presentation of a displaced femoral neck fracture. Given the high-energy mechanism of a rear-end collision and the specific deformity, I suspect this is a displaced fracture with potential vascular compromise. Can you tell me if you are able to move your toes or feel sensation in your foot? REQUEST IMAGES: X_Ray_Right_Hip
